newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvian c.bank cancels licence of small bank.
newsitem.headline: Latvian c.bank cancels licence of small bank.

text.p: Latvia's central bank said on Friday it had decided to cancel the licence of Latvijas Privatbanka, accusing it of dishonesty.
The central bank said it would request the court to order the liquidation of Privatbanka which it said had broken banking laws and central bank rules.
"With Latvijas Privatbanka we have encountered dishonest work for a long time," the bank said in a statement.
Latest data show that Privatbanka was Latvia's 27th largest bank out of 33 functioning banks with assets of 7.3 million lats and share capital of 1.10 million lats.
This compares with the assets of top bank Parex Bank of 173.5 million lats and own capital of 25.66 million lats.
The central bank has been tightening regulations and supervision of banks to bring the sector back to full health after a damaging bank crisis in mid-1995.
Many banks are not allowed to accept deposits from inviduals and all have to meet tight requirements on reporting.
But the central bank said that Privatbanka was guilty of performing operations for which it was not licensed, such as taking in deposits from individuals.
It also misinformed the central bank by giving wrong information about its share capital and work abroad and also broke book-keeping regulations.
The central bank said that the liquidation of Privatbanka would not have a big impact on companies, people or the economy but would be a positive factor.
"Dishonest banks can have a negative impact on the prestige of the bank system and potential investor interest in Latvia," the central bank said.
"Therefore, cancelling the licence of Latvijas privatbanka will have not a negative but rather a positive impact on the whole bank sector," it added.
